channel.title: EngineerzCorneR — Posts
channel.description: Deep-dive technical write-ups across Electrical, Mechanical, HVAC, Automation, Civil and Solar.

item.title: Basics of Fire Protection in Buildings Explained
item.description: Passive protection, active systems, detection, suppression and safe evacuation — the five layers of building fire protection, how sprinklers, hydrants, fire pumps and alarm systems work together, and the simple working sequence from detection to fire brigade response.

item.title: BOD & BOP in Pipe Bending: The Key to Piping Take-Off & Fabrication
item.description: BOD (Bend Outside Diameter) and BOP (Bend Center Line) are the two dimensions that drive piping material take-off and fabrication. Formulas, a bend allowance table, and a worked 2-inch 90° bend example.

item.title: Earthing vs. Grounding: Same Earth Connection, Different Job
item.description: Earthing and grounding both connect to earth, but their purpose is different — earthing protects people from shock, grounding protects the electrical system. Purpose, connection point, current flow and where each is used, compared.

item.title: Erosional vs. Economic Velocity: Which One Actually Sizes Your Pipe?
item.description: Two different velocity limits compete to size a process line — economic velocity minimizes lifecycle cost, the API RP 14E erosional velocity protects the pipe wall. The lower of the two always governs.

item.title: Facility & Property Management: Key Codes & Standards Reference
item.description: The key codes and standards that govern facility and property management — maintenance, HVAC, fire & life safety, occupational health, electrical, building codes, and more.

item.title: Facility Management: Monthly Invoice Processing
item.description: How FM teams process monthly invoices — the 3 expense categories (utility, service, consumables), the 10-step verification-to-filing workflow, and a worked invoice tracker example.

item.title: FM-200 System Diagram: Components & How It Works Explained
item.description: FM-200 clean agent fire suppression system explained — cylinder, solenoid valve, nozzles, control panel, detection system, manual release station and pressure switch, with a full system diagram and how each part triggers discharge.

item.title: Gas Detector Types & Working Principles Explained
item.description: Catalytic bead, electrochemical, infrared, semiconductor and photoionization (PID) gas detectors compared — what each senses, how the sensing element actually works, and where each type is applied.

item.title: Icw, Icu, Ics & Icm Explained: Four kA Ratings, Four Different Jobs
item.description: Four short-circuit kA ratings on a breaker or busbar nameplate — Icw, Icu, Ics and Icm — and what each one actually certifies, with a worked example showing how they relate.

item.title: LV Panel Types Explained: Switchgear, MCC, PFC, VFD, Feeder Pillar & More
item.description: Every panel you'll find in a low-voltage electrical system — MDB, PCC, SDB/DB, MCC, VFD panel, APFC/PFC panel, feeder pillar, busbar trunking, ATS/AMF and PLC panels — what each does, where it sits, and the IEC 61439 parts behind it.

item.title: Fire Fighting: NFPA Fire Protection System Design Standards Reference
item.description: A quick-reference table of the NFPA standards that govern fire protection system design — NFPA 10, 13, 14, 16, 17A, 20, 22, 2001 and local civil defense compliance — what each covers and where it applies.

item.title: P&ID Instrument Bubbles: Line Types & Tag Anatomy Explained
item.description: What the line under an instrument bubble actually means — field-mounted, control-room-mounted, or not directly accessible — plus how to break down a tag like TT01 into loop number, measured variable and device function using ISA S5.1.

item.title: P&ID (Piping & Instrumentation Diagram) Explained
item.description: How to actually read a P&ID — equipment, piping, valves, instrumentation tags, and signal lines — plus the ISA tag-naming logic and how a P&ID differs from a PFD.

item.title: Pipe Routing Guide: 13 Rules Every Layout Should Follow
item.description: Pipe routing principles, pump suction line routing, equipment clearance, pipe racks, supports, dead legs, expansion loops, hot/cold line routing, utility routing, underground vs above ground, nozzle orientation, flange accessibility, and maintenance clearances.

item.title: PLC vs DCS vs SCADA Explained: Real Industrial Comparison
item.description: PLC, DCS and SCADA compared for real industrial use — control type, speed, architecture, redundancy, and where control execution actually happens — plus a feature-by-feature table and typical applications for each.

item.title: Power System Protection Relays: The Complete Reference Guide
item.description: Every protection relay category in one place — operation workflow, the five design goals, current/voltage/distance/differential/frequency relays, IEC 61850 architecture, inverse-time curves, coordination principles and a quick selection table.

item.title: Power Transformer, CT & PT: Internal Construction
item.description: The internal construction of a power transformer, a current transformer (CT), and a potential transformer (PT/VT) — parts, typical ratings, accuracy classes, and a side-by-side comparison.

item.title: Pre-Commissioning vs Commissioning: What's the Difference
item.description: Pre-commissioning happens before a system is energized; commissioning happens after. The checks each phase actually covers, why the order matters, and where FAT and SAT fit in.

item.title: Conventional vs. Balanced Bellows vs. Pilot-Operated PSV: Choosing a Relief Valve Type
item.description: Three ways a pressure relief valve holds its disc shut until set pressure — how back pressure, operating margin, and dirty service tolerance decide between a conventional, balanced bellows, or pilot-operated PSV.

item.title: Relay Basics: Construction, Working Principle & Contact Types
item.description: What a relay actually is, how the coil and armature switch a separate power circuit, NO/NC/CO contact types, a control-vs-power circuit diagram, common applications, key specs, and the trade-offs versus contactors and solid-state relays.

item.title: SCADA (Supervisory Control & Data Acquisition) Explained
item.description: How SCADA actually works — the field/communication/supervisory architecture, the 5-step monitor-to-action loop, components, communication protocols, SCADA system types, and SCADA vs DCS compared.

item.title: Star (Y) and Delta (Δ) Connections Explained
item.description: How Star (Y) and Delta (Δ) three-phase winding connections actually differ — the neutral point, the line/phase voltage and current relationships, terminal wiring, and why a Star-Delta starter switches between the two.

item.title: How to Calculate & Select Supply Air Terminal & Return Air Terminal
item.description: How to calculate supply and return air terminal quantity from room CFM — diffuser CFM/NC/throw selection, return grille face velocity, air balance, and a full worked example with layout.

item.title: Tap Changer of a Distribution Transformer Explained
item.description: How an off-load tap changer adjusts a distribution transformer's turns ratio to keep output voltage in range — where it sits, how tap positions map to voltage, and a worked ±5% example.

item.title: Types of Earthing Systems: 9 Electrode Types Explained
item.description: Nine types of earthing electrodes explained — plate, pipe, rod, strip, wire, chemical, ring, mesh and equipment earthing — with what each is built from and where it's actually used.

item.title: Types of HVAC Fans
item.description: The five main HVAC fan types compared — axial, centrifugal, inline, mixed-flow and exhaust fans. How each one works, typical applications and key advantages, so you can match the fan to the job.

item.title: UPS Architecture, Types & Operating Modes Explained
item.description: How an online double-conversion UPS is built — rectifier/charger, battery bank, inverter, static switch and bypass — the three operating modes, offline vs line-interactive vs online UPS types, and key protections and parameters.

item.title: WTI vs OTI Explained: Winding vs Oil Temperature Indicators
item.description: WTI (Winding Temperature Indicator) vs OTI (Oil Temperature Indicator) on a power transformer — what each measures, how WTI simulates hot-spot temperature using a CT-fed heating element, a worked example, and why both alarms matter.

item.title: Earthing & Grounding Systems Explained: Why Resistance Is the Whole Game
item.description: What an earthing system is actually protecting against, why grid resistance is the number that matters, the factors that drive it.

item.title: Sag in Transmission Lines Explained
item.description: What sag is in an overhead transmission line, why it's designed in rather than eliminated, the level-support sag formula, the factors that raise or lower it, typical sag-to-span ratios by voltage level, and why sag is checked at multiple temperatures.
